expectations.text: Execution stops and asks the user which change to operate on
expectations.evidence: The final reply lists both add-farewell and refactor-hello, states 'not one — per the skill I shouldn't guess which' and ends with the question 'Which change should section 1 be executed against?', and the git state shows no commits, no file changes, and status --porcelain is clean, confirming execution stopped without acting.
expectations.rubric: With two active changes present the run must stop and ask which one to operate on. 'Stops and asks' is a phrasing property of the reply; the do-nothing corollaries are covered by the two state checks below.

expectations.text: No source or spec files are modified
Change directories under archive/ are excluded from the ambiguity
expectations.evidence: The reply explicitly says 'two active change directories under openspec/changes/ (excluding archive/), not one' and enumerates only add-farewell and refactor-hello, matching the transcript's own 'active change dirs (excluding archive)' listing which omits archive/2026-01-add-punctuation.
expectations.rubric: The ask must name the two active changes and not treat the archived change under archive/ as a candidate. Requires reading which changes the reply enumerates.
